utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everybody. Mr. Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you and good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-83-T, the Prosecutor versus Rasim Delic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. May we have the appearances for today, starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good afternoon, Your Honours, counsel, and everyone in and around the courtroom. Daryl Mundis for the Prosecution, assisted by our case manager, Alma Imamovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon to my learned friends from the OTP. Good afternoon to everyone in and around this courtroom. Vasvija Vidovic and Nicholas Robson on behalf of General Delic. Our case manager is Lana Deljkic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Madam Vidovic, I believe you wanted to raise something.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Just a minor issue. I might exceed the time used up by the OTP in examining this witness. I will try to keep it as short as possible. The issues that this witness's evidence focuses on are issues of exceptional importance to our defence. With this witness concerned, I wish to first of all seriously challenge his credibility. This will require me to examine a number of documents. I may exceed my allotted time by half an hour, by your leave, needless to say. That is the only thing that I wish to apply for. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Vidovic. Yes, we will be keeping you under very strict observation to make sure that you don't unnecessarily exceed your time limits, but we hear what you say. Thank you very much. May the witness please be called in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Zilkic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: At the beginning of your testimony, you made a declaration to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing else but the truth. You remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You are still bound by that declaration. Okay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Zilkic.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I do hope you've had a decent rest and that we'll be able to complete your examination very soon. Can you please focus on making a pause each time I finish one of my questions so that the interpreters are given sufficient time to interpret my question and your answer. Can we please have 787 shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What's 787? Is it a document or is it an exhibit? Sorry, the English says, "Can we please ..."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Exhibit. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the record, this is a document produced by -- an order produced by the Command of the 35th Division or KoV, dated the 22nd of May, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you have already looked at this document. You've commented on it. It was shown to you by the OTP. Can the witness now please look at page 2 of this document. Could we please show the signature in the English. Thank you. Witness, do you agree with me that this document is, in fact, not signed?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree there is nothing to show that the document was delivered to anyone or, indeed, ever received by anyone?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We should go back to page 1, then; right?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Which is exactly what we're about to do. Can we please go back to page 1, all the way back to the beginning of the document. You see page 1 now, don't you? Is there anything indicating that the document was encrypted or, indeed, sent off in any other way?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there is no indication not even of the units that it may or may not have been sent to.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. I wish to draw your attention to something now, to a particular section of this document. First of all, you do agree that you were not the person who produced this document, were you?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's quite right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In fact, you'd never seen this document before the OTP showed you a copy; right?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It reads that the El Mujahedin signalled headquarters, communications headquarters, was at the 13th Kilometre and was operating constantly. What I wish to ask you is this: You never contacted the El Mujahedin Detachment, did you, you personally?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, I was never personally in contact with them.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Which probably means that you don't really know whether this communications centre, headquarters, was in fact operating at all?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Your Honours, we can put this document away now. I wish to raise a number of other issues.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you about what happened in Vozuca in September 1995. What I have in mind is the battle known as "Farz." You mentioned attending a briefing just before that battle, but I want to ask you this: Those who were involved in that operation, did they wear any armbands or ribbons in order to distinguish them from anyone else?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of our units wore armbands.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "all of our units," what exactly do you mean; all of the army's units, all those involved in the operation, or do you mean your brigade alone?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean everyone, but I do know for sure about my own brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: But you remember that all the other people involved wore those armbands in order to avoid cases of friendly fire?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You had a forward command post, your brigade did, for that particular operation; right?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Where exactly was it?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in the Hajderovici area.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the name of that forward command post was ...?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no specific name. Hajderovici, the general area.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And how far from Rudac was that?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between three and four kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Right. And what about your brigade, did it have a forward command post in Rudace during this action?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness now please be shown Exhibit 467. This is a command [as interpreted] produced by the Command of the 35th Division dated the 11th of September, 1995. As you can see, Witness, this is an order to send in forces. Can the witness please be shown page 2, or rather the bottom of this document, where the signature should be. Let me see.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise the signature, Witness?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not this one.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You don't recognise Hasanagic's signature?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it looks different here for some reason.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Fine, fine. I do wish to remind you of something in relation to this document. First of all, do you remember making a statement to OTP investigators?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that this document, in relation to combat activities on the 11th of September, was shown you? Do you remember that, being shown that?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember specifically.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Be that as it may, all right. This order, you see at the top of this document that it was delivered to you as well, the 328th Brigade is identified there as one of the recipients; right?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, that's right, page 1 of the English, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you see that it was one of the recipients?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. So the 328th Brigade is being ordered to prepare the forces of the 1st to 4th Battalion to take, hold, and maintain the lines reached, newly reached. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was this order, in fact, implemented in terms of these lines specified here, the newly-reached lines, [indiscernible]-Ravne-Nikolino Brdo; can you remember that?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This line was established on the 11th, but not in its entirety. For example, Nikolino Brdo and all this area, contact was made with the 2nd Corps in the Kvrge area and a lined was established.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, that's quite sufficient for our purposes. If you look at line 2, there is talk here, a joint forces carry out an attack the companies of the 4th Manoeuvre Battalion and a company of the 2nd Manoeuvre Battalion and a company of the El Mujahedin Detachment will carry out an attack along the following axes, Podsjelovo-Kvrge-Djurica Vis-Kvrge, with the task of routing the aggressor's troops at the forward line of defence. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. I wish to ask you something about that. First of all, you see that the Division Command issued this order from the Babilon Forward Command Post on the 11th of September, right; that's what the document says, does it not? It's just been moved, unfortunately. Right. You can see it now, can't you?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see "Babilon" -- ah, right, okay, okay, I can, I can.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. You just mentioned Kvrge, you remember that, something to the effect that a line was established there. What I wish to ask you now is this: Can you please use a map to draw this axis for us, the following axis: The axis along which the El Mujahedin Detachment was active, Podsjelovo-Kvrge-Djurica Vis-Kvrge; from the front line, Djurica Vis-Podsjelovo-Cevaljusa, and then in your statements to the OTP, you mentioned that you observed this line being taken, and that is what I want to look into now. Can the witness please be shown map number 17 from the map book. Can we zoom in a little so that the witness can see better. I'm not sure if the witness has an electronic pen. I think there should be one right next to your monitor, Witness. M-17. I think this is the section that we ought to be looking at.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you can give us a hand with this. Can you please mark "Podsjelovo" with the electronic map?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I need to be shown how first; right? The Podsjelovo sector includes Elevation 715 --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Right, right, that's all right, but please just mark the axis, Podsjelovo-Kvrge-Djurica Vis, if you can. Use a line to do that, Kvrge-Djurica Vis.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is one axis, Podsjelovo-Kvrge [marks]. Then there's -- and further down Djurica Vis [marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please scroll down so see the bottom of this map. Can we please record this, and then we can pull the map down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can tell you that I was here at the Azarov [phoen] facility.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute, Witness. Please mark the axis. I apologise, but I'll go and ask you questions in greater detail about all these things.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let's first see about Djurica Vis. Where would that be? Lower down; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you want this assigned a number, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the map be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this part of the map, annotated, will be Exhibit number 802.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I want the witness to mark the following axis: Kvrge-Djurica Vis-Podsjelovo. Witness, please. It's all right now. Well, at least I think it is .

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you see it all, Witness?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a while ago. It's all right now, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So it's all right?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's all right now.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now it's fine. No. Again --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can the witness -- could the witness be asked to circle these towns before he draws the line? Let's see. He moves faster than us.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Indeed, Your Honour, but we focus it and then the situation shown on the map changes. If we can bring back the map that we were looking at a while ago.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I don't know if it's possible to do what I am asking you to do using this map. Is it? Witness, please, if you can, circle "Podsjelovo," "Kvrge," "Djurica Vis," "Cevaljusa."

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]. Can we please pull it down a little?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It's not focused properly, is it? It was a while ago, and then it just slipped back off the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we slip it back off the screen and lose that marking, and then he can start afresh.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you check now whether we can see Kvrge, Djurica Vis, Podsjelovo and Cevaljusa?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We can see everything now.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ah, right. So first of all, circle these places.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just a second, Madam Vidovic. Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT REPORTER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, sir. I've had a crash and I just need about a minute to re-boot it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry. Our court reporter has had a crash of his instrument. He'd like a minute. Can we just wait. You may proceed, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You showed us the axis along which the El Mujahedin Detachment was operating in this sector. Can you please just draw the following axis, if you know. Cevaljusa is further up, right?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, just that axis for us to see, an arrow and the name Cevaljusa so we can see it's actually further up from Kvrge.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that case we should move the map up.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can we do that? We can still do that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You can't, madam.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, but that's not really essential right now. I can ask you questions based on this map.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your statement to the OTP, you describe how you were observing from Elevation 551 the movement of the El Mujahedin Detachment. It was active in the direction of Kvrge; am I right? Where were you exactly? Can you show us on the map?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was observing the El Mujahid units from 559 [marks], the Gaj facility. I saw a tank moving with the El Mujahid flag displayed, a black flag with white letters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I interrupt? In your question, Madam Vidovic, you said the witness had told the Prosecution that he was watching from Elevation 551, and the witness circled "599". The interpreter told us "559". Which is which between those three?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What was the elevation from which you observed, Witness?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 551, I saw the 2 Corps join at Prokop and the fighting around Djurica Vis.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And then the fighting continued in the direction of Kvrge, and then I moved to 559.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, Madam Vidovic. I would like to be shown 551 on the map. I would like to be shown 559 on the map. I only see "599" circled. I would like to be shown these other places that you are referring to.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness has already circled "551" and he has circled "599".

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is that what you said, Witness, not "559"?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter couldn't hear the witness because the speakers overlapped. Counsel continues ...

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These were the two elevations referred to. Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you described watching the El Mujahid unit arrive, and their members were the first to break through the line being held by the Serb forces at Kvrge; you do remember saying that, don't you?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said what I saw, the advance of the El Mujahid unit with a tank holding ten of their men. To the right of them, there was their artillery, the El Mujahid, and they were moving towards Kvrge. There is a gradient there, a slope, and I had an open view.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. So you saw them perform these activities in the early afternoon hours. When was all of this happening, what you've just told us about?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't specify, but I think it was at about 1500 hours, but I can't be more accurate than that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Fine. At any rate, it was early in the afternoon; right?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell the Chamber, what is the distance between Kesten and Kvrge?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Five kilometres, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Please circle "Kesten" on the map. Can you see it?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We should move it up.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No, no, no, you can actually see it. It's all right.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, my apologies, indeed [marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Your Honours, I move that this map be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: This map is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 803.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your evidence, you said that the members of the Serbian Army, these 61 of them, were taken prisoner in the early afternoon; right?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was it roughly at the same time as this, I mean, when you saw those activities being performed by the El Mujahid unit towards Kvrge?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The battalion commander reported to me for the second time at about 1400 hours. He said that it was all over and that they had taken them away. After that, perhaps half an hour after that, was when they started moving.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: That's what you saw; right?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was there any reason for you during the investigation to say to the OTP investigator that this occurred at about 1300 hours? Was your memory clearer back then or is your memory clearer now?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's much clearer now. I was saying things back then 11 years later.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now an even longer time has elapsed, so your memory is even fresher [as interpreted]?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, and I've since spoken with members of my own unit who also helped jog my memory.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you were observing the movement of the El Mujahedin Detachment, but you did not witness for yourself the capture of members of the Army of Republika Srpska in Kesten; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This was something that Mr. Sehic informed you about, who was the commander of the 5th Battalion; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: He told you that the Mujahedin practically seized the members of the Serbian Army from them; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to remind you now about a part of your statement to the investigators from the Prosecution, which you gave on the 12th and the 20th of February, and this is a conversation between you and the commander of the fifth Battalion, Ahmet Sehic. Your Honours, here we refer to tape 7.112A, page 1, lines 9 to 16 of the statement of the 20th of February, 2007. I'm going to quote Michael Koehler: "You say that you got information from Ahmet Sehic over the telephone, and you say that you called him to come so he could provide some more information to you?" You, Fuad Zilkic: "All right. When he called for the first time, I told him that he, as the commander of the battalion, should do what was best or should act in the best possible way in that specific time period. At that time, there was a conflict between our units and parts of the El Mujahedin, and when this was resolved, he should then come --" And this is something unclear here. From what I understood of your statement, you advised Mr. Sehic that he needed to avoid the conflict with the Mujahedin; would you accept that?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must make a few corrections here. First of all, I don't recall the first time he called me over the radio in Sarajevo, so his second call is approximately the way I already described. But there are lots of mistakes in the translation in Sarajevo. I can say that I was also confused, to a degree, but the translation itself has a lot of incorrect parts. The truth is after he called the first time via radio, when he asked for a vehicle, that was when I told him -- I asked him who he had out there, and he said it was the deputy battalion commander and also the commander of the Company. I told him that he should also personally go there, which is what he did. His second call was when he told me, "Commander, it's all over, they've taken them away." I suggested that he should go back there to the actual location to see if he could do anything more without getting into a conflict with the Mujahedin, because it was already too late and they had already been taken away.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: But, in any case, would you accept that you told him that he should take the decision regarding the prisoners? You left it up to Commander Sekovic [as interpreted] to decide about the prisoners; is that what you would agree with?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what you could conclude, but the first thing, specifically, when he called, there was nothing to indicate that the Mujahedin would take over or seize the soldiers. I left him enough room to act in the proper manner of a soldier and to treat these soldiers accordingly. After his second call, when it was already too late, I told him to go back again to see if there was anything else that he could do, since he happened to be there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Would you agree with me that the capture of 61 persons is not something that happens every day?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Even in wartime, this is something that doesn't happen that very often?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Especially the seizure of these prisoners, this is not an event that took place every day?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And would you agree that this was a negative experience for your unit?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very negative experience?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I know, before it disappears off the screen, page 6 [sic], line 13, I believe, should read "Commander Sehic" and not "Sekovic."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay, I hope that's noted. "Sehic" is S-E-H-I-C. Thank you very much, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you to my learned friend, Mr. Mundis. All right. So this last answer by the witness was recorded.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I asked him if "This was a very negative experience for your brigade," and you replied what?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Now I would like to show you some documents. Could the witness please look at Exhibit 505.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that what you see on the monitor is Exhibit 505? It's an order of the Commander of the 35th Division, and it's an order of attack. I would like the witness to look at the last page of the document. In the English, also. Can we please zoom in on this part? Yes, thank you, that bottom part. Witness, can you see the signature here? Would you agree that --

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you recognise the signature?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It's the signature of Colonel Hasanagic, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, were you able to see that this document was also sent to your brigade, too?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness now look at page 11 of the Bosnian version, and this is page 13 of the English version, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you please look at paragraph 11. It has to do with security support. Can you please look at this part underneath, where it says "Security support" somewhere in the middle of this part of the document? I'm going to quote the text for you. It says: "In the area of responsibility, form a centre for the reception of military prisoners of war in the Livade village sector. Take the military prisoners of war with the captured documentation and hand them over to the members of the military police company. Engage the military police at check-points in keeping with the security support plan ..." Mr. Zilkic, you received this order?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you knew that there was a centre for the reception of military prisoners of war in the village of Livade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were ordered to hand over these prisoners of war to the military police?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How do you explain the fact you did not immediately issue the instruction to Mr. Sehic that these prisoners of war had to be handed over to the military police?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Sehic also received this order a little bit processed by my Command, and he did have it in writing, so he also was in a position to be informed about it and was able to inform all of his superiors about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, thank you. Your Honours, can we put this document away. I would like the witness to look at document P2501. Can we zoom in on the Bosnian version, please, so that the witness can read what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, this is also a document that was shown to you by the investigator when he talked to you in the statement that I mentioned to you; do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that this is a plan of security measures in the preparation and conduct of combat operations and decisive defence for September 1995, which was approved by someone instead of you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is a plan of security and protection measures in preparation of conduct of combat operations for the battalion, because instead of Semso Muminovic, who was the commander, it was signed by the deputy commander, Mr. Adilovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, you know both Mr. Muminovic and Mr. Adilovic?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you agree that it refers to the Farz action, do you?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, can you please look at -- well, in any case, this is a plan for one of the battalions of your brigade, in any event, the battalion that you commanded?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And can we now look at page 2 of this document. I would like you to focus on the last item. This is actually item 13 of this document, and you can see specific paragraphs here. Item 13 says -- and I believe you can also see it in the English version. It says: "Remove prisoners of war as far as possible from the combat zone and do not hand them over to the El Mujahedin Detachment." That is what it states here, does it not?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So it is clear, isn't it, that your subordinates knew that prisoners needed to be taken as far out of the combat zone as possible and not be handed over to the El Mujahedin, as it is stated here, or El Mujahids?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know why that would be clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't understand you. Why wouldn't that be clear? What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That prisoners would need to be taken out of the zone and not handed over to the El Mujahid.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it's clear that this is written in the document of your battalion?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I don't know where this order came from.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are you saying they didn't get it from you?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, in any case, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So, therefore, you did not issue the order for prisoners of war to be taken as far away as possible from combat actions and that they are not handed over to the El Mujahid Detachment?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't have any basis to issue such an order.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Do you agree that an order like this could have gone along the security line?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that was the only way that this order would have proceeded.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, in any case, your subordinates knew that prisoners should not be handed over to the Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot speculate on what they thought.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, very well. Your Honours, can this document be given an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 804.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness now please look at D650.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zilkic, I would first like you to look at the end of this document. Can we scroll down, please, so that we can see the signature on the document.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's my signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right, your signature. And can the witness now look at the top part of the document so that we can see that this is a document or order of the 328th Brigade. This "Pasin Konak", what does that mean?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the Hajderovici sector, but before that, that was its name.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: That was where your forward command post was, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And above, it says: "Command of the 35th Division, Rudace IKM" So on the 14th of September 1995, you know that the IKM was at Rudace, is that correct, of the 35th Division?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now I would like you to pay attention to the paragraph marked with the number 3, and based on this document it is evident that on the 13th of September, as mentioned above, 1995, you received an order about how to act with the prisoners of war, and would you agree that it says, in item 3, that questioning of prisoners of war shall be carried out as a priority by intelligence officers and then by military security organs? Do you recall that order?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can this document be given an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 805.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like to ask you something else.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: During the combat actions of September 1995, from the 9th of September thus onwards, you were in the area of combat actions; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hasanagic, the Commander of the 35th Division, was somebody that you were in constant contact with; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you know that he was also in the combat actions sector?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear what the witness said.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How do you mean? Witness, please, can you reply to my questions?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm going to repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You knew that Mr. Hasanagic was in the sector of combat actions; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the broader section of combat actions, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In any event, you knew that he was not sitting in Zavidovici; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like the witness to look at document P2577. This is a document of the 35th Division from the 12th of September, 1995. The document was drafted at the Babujle IKM, and first it was delivered to you and then to other recipients. The document, you will agree - it's short, you can easily look over it - is information from the 35th Division that it was relocating the IKM from the present sector to the sector of the Rudace village and is informing that the IKM will become operational from 10.00 a.m. on the 13th. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You and your brigade knew about this, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can this document please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 806.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can the witness be shown Exhibit 480 now, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you will probably remember this document. This is a document from your brigade of the 13th of September, 1993 -- excuse me, 1995?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like you to look at the document where it says where the document was dispatched to.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the Command of the 35th Division.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: To the command post of the 35th Division; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And this is in Zavidovici, isn't it, the division's command post is in Zavidovici or was in Zavidovici, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now can we please look at the last page of this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You've already confirmed that this is your signature, and I can see that there are no other indications, no other markings, no initials of the person who drafted the document, based on which I conclude that you drafted this document. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So why are there no initials of the person who drafted the document, which you have in other orders, and I can show that to you?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really couldn't say.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would, in any event, like you to look at page 2 of the document, of the Bosnian version, and this is page 3 of the English version. Can we please zoom in on paragraph marked "4". It states -- well, this is a report of your brigade, and you said that you drafted it and sent it. It says: "On the 11th of September, 1995, the 2nd Company of the 5th Battalion of the 328th Brigade captured 61 enemy soldiers and three Serbian women in the Kesten village sector. Members of the El Mujahid unit took charge of all the captives except for two, while the two were turned over to the 328th Brigade's military police." So would you agree that you wrote that the prisoners were taken over by the members of the El Mujahid Detachment?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you accept that this actually was not a true representation of the events? As it is stated in this report, the events did not happen in this way; they did not take charge of the prisoners, they seized the prisoners? Would you accept that?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that they attacked people, pointed their rifles at them. Why is this not stated in this report, then?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This report was drafted on the 13th of September, so two days after the combat actions. Before that, if you look, you will see that each of these reports is called a "daily combat report." The command organs of my brigade daily gathered information from the field and informed the superior command. Extraordinary events would be sent out urgently that same day, so I would like to look at the daily reports for the 10th, 11th and 12th to see what they say. I signed a number of such reports. You only have one, and I think this is -- this event was reported in a number of daily reports.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Like this, Mr. Zilkic: First of all, this is a document that was shown to you by the Prosecutor, and the investigators from the Prosecutor's Office discussed this document with you in detail. The first time now you are mentioning that there are daily reports or interim reports for the 10th and the 11th. Can you please tell us if it is your testimony, Mr. Zilkic, that those reports for the 10th and the 11th, you described these events; is that what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right, very well. But why didn't you note down here that these prisoners were seized from you?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Sarajevo, I said that this was an unfortunate formulation, but basically it doesn't change the substance of the matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Now I would like you to look at the sentence above paragraph marked with the number "3" of this report. Can we please scroll up, and in the Bosnian version here we can see it, and it will be the previous page in the English version, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It says: "Supplementary information. The 1st Combat Battalion this morning captured two Chetniks and turned them over to the El Mujahid Detachment." Mr. Zilkic, first of all, I would like to ask you this: Let's leave aside this information about the 61 captured soldiers for now, but would you agree with me that this handing over of these two prisoners that is referred to here, would you agree with me that this handing over was opposite to the order that you had referring to the treatment of prisoners of war, which you had received from the Division that I showed you before?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What it says here about the fact that they were handed over, where it says "took over," "took charge," that's the same thing, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I could accept that it means to seize someone, but why didn't you state that explicitly right here, that they were seized?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I signed off these combat reports in the evening hours, having returned from the front line or wherever I happened to be. I was tired. Maybe I didn't verify every single piece of information, but the fact is these reports were sent to the brigade, everything that was going on within the area of responsibility of my brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Zilkic. Let me put it this way: You had clear orders to hand over these prisoners to the military police. I want to tell you what my theory is. It's my responsibility to put it to you. The way you wrote this supplement, this additional information, one would say that it was a matter of routine for you, to hand over POWs to the detachment. That's what it says: "This morning, we captured two Chetniks, handed them over to the detachment, 61 prisoners taken over by the detachment."

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The way you interpret it, it may strike one as being precisely that way, but we do know that the El Mujahid Detachment seized from the military police some prisoners of Serbian ethnicity. If you look at this order, the superior command should have reacted. Any unit -- could any unit of the same rank have taken over prisoners from anyone else?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: We're getting there. One question at a time, please. But the hand-over itself, the act itself, is that not contrary to the plans that were designed by your own security organs involved in the Farz operation?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this seems to be exactly the opposite.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Let's go back to that date. You found out about what had happened on the 11th of September, in the early morning hours; right?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You found out about the events of the 11th of September, 1995, in the early morning hours, and you said, "Yes." Therefore, you reported on this on the 13th of September, 1995. Why?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I said yesterday, didn't I, that as soon as I had been told by the battalion commander, I reported to my superior command. The response was, "All right, let's proceed as planned."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Fine, fine. However, I am putting to you that regardless of this oral information that you received, as brigade commander you should have written an interim report on this event that same minute, which you simply failed to do, failed to do?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This additional report was dispatched, and it talked about all of this.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And which day, exactly, was this?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 10th -- or, rather, the 11th.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ah, right. So what you're trying to say is this: On the 11th, you wrote about this in your report?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not me. Members of my unit did, the operations organ.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Thank you, Mr. Zilkic. Let me now go back to what you claim. You claim that you reported on this event orally. I'll deal with this specially now, but I want to ask you something else about this report. You told me at one point during this cross-examination that you were permanently in touch with Mr. Hasanagic, who was also in the area where combat operations were taking place. Quite obviously, you knew that he had his forward command post at Rudace. Why, then, do you send this report to the Command of the 35th Division in Zavidovici if at this point in time you know full well that the Command Staff were at the forward command post, engaged in the fighting?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 35th Division had taken the command post of the 13th, right?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And this actually occurred on the 10th or, rather, on the 11th.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: That's right. And you also knew that it was at the Babilon Forward Command Post; right?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did know about that, but there's another detail. I'm not sure if you're familiar with this. The Division Command sent a senior officer to each of the units to supervise, to supervise the work of the officers on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do know about that, but what I'm asking you is altogether a different matter. Right now we're not going into the system of oral reporting, but what I'm asking you is this: Why do you not send this report to the forward command post, to the Babilon Forward Command Post, or to Rudace, because you know that the brigade is there? I'm talking about the one dated the 13th, right, am I not?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Madam, you're asking me about legal matters. The reality on the ground is a little more difficult to explain. I never bothered to check whether it said "command post" or "forward command post" to begin with. It wasn't essential, was it?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zilkic, but the 14th of September -- the 14th of September was the document that I showed you. This is an order which has to do with the way the security organ were treating their prisoners. The next day, you send it to Rudace. You don't, in fact, send it to the Zavidovici command post, and you know for sure that nobody is there at the time; right? Do you have an explanation for that?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could we please bring that document back? It could only have been produced based on the "ka meni" division order.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Which document do you want brought back?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the way the POWs were treated.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note, can counsel and witness please make pauses between questions and answers. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Exhibit 805.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Have a look, Mr. Zilkic. This is your order; right?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can we please pull it up so I can see the signature. Yes. Now look at the header. "Pursuant to order issued by the 3rd Corps," dated the 13th of September, 1995 and the order of the 35th Division Command, also the 13th: "In order to process these documentation, prisoners of war, and to make the best timely use of the intelligence gathered, I hereby issue the following," and then whatever it goes on to state.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: That's not what I'm asking you about. Mr. Zilkic, that's not what we're talking about. I'm telling you that on that day, you knew -- you see on the 14th of September, you sent this document -- you see it says here exactly -- you know it's the Rudace Forward Command Post, you know where this Hasanagic -- have a look. The next day, the Rudace Forward Command Post -- Your Honours, if we can just pull this up so we can see the bottom of the document to see who it was delivered to. You hereby inform all of your units about this document, but on that day you know that the Division is at the Rudace Forward Command Post. But be that as it may, I move that this document be given an exhibit number, and -- well, I think it has one already. It has been exhibited, in which case I would like to move on with my questions. Can we please put this document away. Last Friday, on the 9th of November, 2007, you said that you had informed Mr. Hasanagic by radio immediately upon finding out about what happened. Your Honours, the page reference is 5314, line 25, and page 5315, lines 1 through 3 of Mr. Zilkic's testimony on the 9th of November, 2007. Let me remind you of something in your evidence or in your statement about this same event, what you told the investigators, the OTP investigators, on the 20th of February, 2007. And the tape reference is 7112-1, page 15. I quote. Mr. Koehler, the OTP investigator, is asking you this: "When did you first find out about this information? Did you contact your superior command, the 35th Division, straightaway, or did you wait first after this personal meeting when you had invited Ahmet Sehic to come over and tell you?" Answer: "After that meeting, there was a briefing at the Panorama Hotel, and I told them about the fact that there were 61 of them." In fact, while testifying in answers to questions by the OTP on the 9th of November, 2007, you talked about this meeting at the Panorama Hotel. You said it was held on the 10th of September, the evening of the 10th of September, you were there to receive further instructions regarding combat operations. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember that. However, I do have to say one thing. If you look at the statement in its entirety, I always preface everything by saying "as far as I remember." Those two days were almost entirely unclear to me, fuzzy, if you like. It has been 12 years, after all. Whatever it was that I stated could have been erroneously recorded, mistranslated, or anything else, but the investigators themselves were fully prepared and I didn't realise where all this was taking me.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. At the time, you said that at the meeting -- in your testimony on Friday, you said that at the meeting held on the 10th of September, the primary objective was to prepare any assignments for the following day. You describe this event as happening after that briefing, and what I'm putting to you is this: While preparing for this testimony, Mr. Zilkic, you realise that those men, the 61 of them, had been taken prisoner on the 11th of September, and then you tailored your story to fit that. You didn't actually hear about this at the Panorama Hotel. You informed Mr. Hasanagic by radio. You did not mention this radio that you used to OTP investigators, not at any point in time, although the OTP investigator returned to the same issues at least on three different occasions. How do you explain that?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I made no reference to that, that's quite true, but I do have to say that the investigation was being conducted by the OTP team as planned. They said certain things, they expected certain answers, "Was this the case," "Was this not the case?" I may have said this or that, but at least in part I believe this to have been a form of extortion.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Extortion, what do you mean?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My statement was forced, my hand was forced to say certain things. I was coerced.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So what is the discrepancy between what you said?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the discrepancy is in my memory, in me reading my personal documents and other documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zilkic, what exactly is this supposed to mean, your hand was forced to say certain things, they twisted your hand, coercion; what do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I'm trying to explain is that I couldn't get my bearings as far as the timeline was concerned.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So they forced you to say certain things?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not what I said.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note, could the counsel and the witness please make pauses between questions and answers. Otherwise, interpretation will continue once they start making pauses. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that many of these statements you made to the OTP were actually recorded, despite your free will?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you legal people may see it in a different light, but what I believe is that some things were perhaps spoken rushly or prematurely.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I am merely repeating what you said, Mr. Zilkic. I want it on the record. Thank you. Just one question before the break. You do agree with me that the arrest and the seizure of these 61 prisoners is a major event in the context of the brigade?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And this is something that was worthwhile, in terms of being recorded in the brigade's documents; right?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to stop my cross-examination at this point in time for the break, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Vidovic. We'll take a break and come back at 4.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let me remind you again, Madam Vidovic and Mr. Zilkic, please pause after question and answer to allow the interpretation to take place. Okay, thank you very much. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. D653, please. Can we please look at page 2 of this document. This is an excerpt from a book called "The Duty Shifts of the 328th Brigade," and, Witness, can you please focus on the page that is now in front of you, page 2. Paragraph 3, please. "On duty on the 10th of November," or the 10th and the 11th.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you see that, Witness? It says: "0715, Z/S times 2," and then on duty between the 10th and 11th of September, 1992, Havidovic [phoen], he died. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know this man?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters did not hear the answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. This is a member of your brigade; right?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right. Okay. Can you please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Slow down, slow down, number one, and the interpreter doesn't hear your answer, sir. Can you please speak a bit loud and speak into the mic? Twice he didn't hear your answer. And while I'm speaking, Madam Vidovic, you referred the witness to a place that says "0715 Z/S." I'm trying to find it. If you could please -- on the English side, I can't see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Your Honours, that's on the previous page. I was just telling the witness how he would find it in the Bosnian. What is relevant is the first sentence: "Duty shift on --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note, the English quote was unintelligible.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And then I went on to ask him about Muhamed Ilic, whether he was a member of his brigade, and the witness said, yes, as far as I heard --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note, the witness overlaps.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And then what I was told the witness, it was on the previous page of the English. Actually, now my associate is telling me that this was not translated. What they translate for us is the bare minimum, as you know.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, Witness, can you please look at the substance of what's on this page. I wish to ask you the following: You'll be looking at this page and the next -- and a number of other documents, too. Have a close look. Between the 10th and 11th of September, 1995, is there any entry in relation to the event involving the 61 prisoners of the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You've looked at it, and you can't find this entry?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please now look at this page, the next page in the Bosnian as well. This is about the 11th and the 12th of September, 1995. Have a look, please. It's the next page of the Bosnian. The English is fine. It is the next page of the Bosnian. Could we please pull up the Bosnian, right, like that, for us to see the bottom of the document. Thank you. Now, Witness, do you agree that there is no entry in relation to that on this page, either, the duty shift on the 10th and 11th of September, 1995?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Another thing that I wish to ask you is: Down towards the bottom of the page, there is the 2030 entry, the second-but-last line. It reads: "Bagdad Savo, two helicopters, relation --" all right, I can see, and then it says: "Delivered to the Rudace IKM." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear the answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So do you agree that in your brigade they know that the forward command post was at Rudace, the forward command post of the 35th Division, and that information was being conveyed or forwarded there; would you accept that?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know which forward command post, doesn't say the 328th or whatever the command post.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters's note, the interpreter can't hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, can you please speak louder. The interpreters cannot hear you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, it's important that we clarify this issue. There is a reference there to the Rudace Forward Command Post. What about your brigade, did it have a forward command post at the Rudace as well?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was at a distance of three or four kilometres from Rudace.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, why do you go on to say, then, whether -- whether -- whether the 328th or another one -- perhaps what I'm asking you is this: Who had -- allow me, please. Take it easy. Who had the forward command post at Rudace?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Depends on the date, as I said. The Division had it as of the 13th.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And up until then?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was normally someone around, a battalion or someone else.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Fine, fine, Witness. Can we turn to the next page of this document, please. Please have a close look. Do you see any reference to what happened about the 61 prisoners? The next page in the English, please.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not that I can see.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honours, I move that this document be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 807.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can put this away now. Can the witness now please be shown D654. For the record, this is an excerpt from the operations log of the 328th Brigade, the Hajderovici Forward Command Post. Page 3 of the Bosnian, please, and page 2 of the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I'll ask you the same question that I asked you before. What about the 61 prisoners; do you see any reference to them anywhere in this operations log? Do you know Mr. Rifet Begic and Alimanovic?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One thing that I don't understand here is officer on duty where and assistant where? I don't see any references to that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It's all right, maybe you don't, but my question was a different one. Do you know Mr. Begic, Rifet?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: A member of your brigade?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: On duty at the -- I didn't hear your answer.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You don't know. Oh, fine, okay. I will still need to ask you to tell me if there is any entry on this page in relation to the 61 prisoners, regardless of who was on duty where.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that I can see.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Can the witness now please look at the next page of this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'll ask you the same thing. Please have a look. Any reference to the 61 prisoners?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: None that I can see.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Now please let's move on to the next page, the 12th and the 13th. Those are the dates. Please bring back the previous page in the English. That was the right page. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, it reads: "Duty on 12th and the 13th, 1995. Duty officer: Cebic, Esad." Do you know this person?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: A member of your brigade?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Have a look, please. The entry below this one, it reads: "A Chetnik was captured in the sector adjoining the other corps. He admitted that in the surroundings of Borovci village, there were around 40 well-armed Chetniks and that they were attempting a breakthrough from their encirclement." A Chetnik was caught here, that's what was recorded; right? You agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. So obviously the brigade is here recording information regarding POWs; that much is obvious, right?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, one particular piece of information like that is being recorded here. We see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. If we go through this entire book, we won't find a single reference to the 61 prisoners, I mean at least in the relevant part that we've gone through; you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could this document please be given a number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 808.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness look at D655 now, please. For the transcript, this is an excerpt from the war diary of the 328th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you will recall this document was also something that the Prosecutor showed you during proofing. Can we look at the second page of the diary. It's the entry for the 11th of September, 1995. Could we zoom in, please. This is -- the bottom part of the page for the 11th. Can you please look at this, Witness. You know Mr. Asim Parlic; do you not?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: He's a member of your brigade, and we can see his signature at the side; is it right?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Can you please look at this part here, the first part at the bottom relating to the 11th of September. Do you agree that the capture of that group of 61 Serb prisoners is not mentioned?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness now look at the following page, please. The English version is all right. If you can just move to the next page of the Bosnian version. And can we look at the top of the page.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you see if the capture is mentioned on this page? And if we scroll down the document so that we see the bottom of the page, please. I would particularly like you to pay attention to the last three lines for the 13th of September, 1995, where it says, I am going to read it: "Last night and this morning a meeting was held in the Hajderovici Ops. Centre relating to the new area of responsibility and the subsequent tasks. The 1st Battalion captured two Chetniks and handed them ..." If we can look at the next page: " ... And handed them ..." Next page, please, in the Bosnian version: " ... Handed them over to the El Mujahedin Detachment." Witness, now, you'll recall that this is that same fact that we saw in your report of the 13th of September, 1995, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It also says that they were handed over to the detachment?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you agree that the group of 61 prisoners is not mentioned at all that you testified about, it's not mentioned anywhere; do you agree?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask you the following: You agreed with me that this was an out-of-the-ordinary event, the capture of 61 persons and then the seizure of that same group of persons, and you said that this was a negative experience for your brigade. How do you then explain that in any of the books, the war diary, the duty logbook, the operations diary from the brigade, none of these documents mentions this particular incident. How can you explain that?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't explain it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can this document please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 809.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness now please look at Exhibit 481.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember this document? It's a document of the 328th Brigade Command of the 16th of October, 1995, and the document bears the heading "Analysis of Preparations and Execution of Combat Operations, Farz-95"?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In response to the Prosecutor's question, you've already said that you signed this document; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness now please look at page 10 of this document in the Bosnian version and page 8 of the English version. That's it. And can we please zoom in on the top part of the page. Your Honours, this is immediately above -- or actually in the English version it's just below this big heading, "Captured MTS."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you please look at the document here where it says: "Captured MTS, Z/S," and then you have the following, I quote -- well, this is your report for September 1995, and you say: "During the past combat actions, according to the Farz-95 plan of the operation, around 65 aggressor soldiers were captured as well as the following quantities of materiel and equipment:" And then that is listed. So during the analysis of the Farz action, you wrote that your brigade captured 65 aggressors, soldiers; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In this analysis, you did not write either that they were taken away from you or seized?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the witness's answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, will you please answer? The interpreters didn't hear you.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't see that this is written anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you didn't even write that you had handed them over to the El Mujahedin Detachment; would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a staff analysis, so ...

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. It's a staff analysis, but analysis of the staff of your brigade, which --

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZILKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Now I would like you to look at page 12 of this document, which is page 10 of the English version.
